newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Over 102,000 seek Moroccan local council seats.
newsitem.headline: Over 102,000 seek Moroccan local council seats.

text.p: More than 102,000 candidates will compete for 24,253 seats in Morocco's local council elections due on June 13, the interior ministry said.
"The number of independent candidates as well as those with a political affiliation totalled 102,400," the Moroccan news agency MAP quoted a ministry statement as saying late on Thursday.
Campaigning for the local elections has been set for the period of May 29 to June 12.
According to the interior ministry 14,447 candidates are standing as independents. The remainder come from 13 political parties. The party with most candidates is the old guard Istiqlal with 14,008.

The four main opposition parties, grouped in a bloc known as the Koutla, are fielding a total of 33,987 candidates. The parties are the Istiqlal, Socialist Union of Peoples Forces (USFP), the Socialist and Progress Party (PPS) and the Organisation of Democratic and Popular Action (OADP).
The Wifaq group of rightwing parties totals 24,079 candidates. They are made up of Constitutional Union (UC), the Popular Movement (MP) and the National Democratic Party (PND).

The local elections are the first of a series which will be capped by a parliamentary poll in September, with a new bicameral parliament being inaugurated by King Hassan on the second Friday of October.
Under the new constitution, the Lower House of parliament will be directly elected through universal suffrage.
Local councils will elect around 80 percent of the members of the new Upper House of Parliament being set up under constitutional reforms approved last September.
The new house will have power to vote a no-confidence motion in the government and could topple it.
